text:
### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A32, A33 and A38 each ran in about 49 in 100 traces and were mutually exclusive with A27 (A27 co-occurred with each of them in essentially no trace; A27 appeared alone in about 52 in 100 traces, each branch activity alone in about 48–49 in 100). In the later window, each of A32, A33 and A38 was observed in only 1 of 200 traces, while A27 ran in about 199 of 200 traces with roughly one occurrence per trace, up from about 52 in 100 traces before. [OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, REL022, REL023, REL024]
- The three branch activities co-occurred with one another in about 48–49 in 100 traces before and in none after (in about 99–100 in 100 traces neither was present), consistent with them forming a single alternative branch. [REL028, REL029, REL030]
- A14, A15, A26 and A28 occurred in every trace in both windows. Before, A14, A15 and A26 each co-occurred with A27 in about 51–52 in 100 traces and with each of A32/A33/A38 in about 48–49 in 100; in the later window they co-occurred with A27 in about 99–100 in 100 traces and practically never with A32/A33/A38. [REL009, REL013, REL017, REL010, REL014, REL018]
- Precedence over A28 flipped: before, A32, A33 or A38 preceded A28 in about 48–49 in 100 traces and A27 preceded it in about 51 in 100; in the later window A27 preceded A28 in about 97 in 100 traces and A28 almost never co-occurred with the branch activities. [REL021, REL025, REL026, REL027]
- Pairs involving the branch activities collapsed to a single observed instance in the later window (for example A26→A32 fell from about 97 observed pairs to 1). [LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009, LAG010]
- A04 fell from about 68 in 100 traces to about 22 in 100 (43 of 200); its relative position moved later and became more dispersed (mean about 0.21 to 0.40, upper quartile about 0.19 to 0.70), and the A14→A04 gap, previously one step in about 99 in 100 of the observed pairs, spread across lags 1–5. [OCC002, POS001, LAG001, REL001]
- Smaller shifts: A02 rose from 5 to 15 in 100 traces and A08 from 5 to about 21 in 100 (both from only about 10 traces before); A14's position shifted slightly later and A28's slightly earlier; A14→A15 became more often immediately consecutive (lag 1 in about 47 in 100 observed pairs versus about 19 before), and A26→A28 concentrated at a gap of two steps (about 95 in 100 versus a mix of gaps 2 and 4 before). [OCC001, OCC003, POS002, POS003, LAG002, LAG003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the alternative branch composed of A32, A33 and A38 — which in the earlier window executed in about half of the cases instead of A27 and preceded A28 — is no longer executed in the later window, leaving the A27 route (A27 executed in virtually every case before A28, alongside A14, A15 and A26) as the only observed route. This is shown directly and consistently: participation of A32, A33 and A38 collapsed from about 49 in 100 traces to 1 of 200 each, A27 rose to near-universal execution, the exclusive-alternative relation between A27 and each branch activity flipped to A27-only, precedence over A28 switched from the branch members to A27, and the pairs with the branch activities fell to a single observation. With 53 control-flow items qualifying against roughly 0.55 expected for an unchanged process, the pattern as a whole cannot be attributed to sampling variation. The evidence cannot distinguish a complete removal of the branch from it still existing but being skipped in almost all cases (it was still observed in 1 of 200 traces), and it cannot indicate why the branch disappeared. [OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL024, REL025, REL026, REL027, LAG004]

Other differences: A04, which previously ran in both routes, dropped from about 68 to about 22 in 100 traces and now occurs later and more variably within the case; A02 and A08 became more frequent (5 to 15 and 5 to about 21 in 100 traces, on small earlier bases); A14's position moved slightly later, A28's slightly earlier, A14→A15 became more often immediately consecutive, and A26→A28 now sits consistently two steps apart. These are not part of the main hypothesis above. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, POS001, POS002, POS003, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]
